title: skellambrms: Skellam and Discrete-Difference brms Custom Families for Count Differences
description:
Custom brms families for the difference between two paired counts, d = y1 - y2, taking values on the integers. Six families are supplied: the symmetric and asymmetric Skellam distributions (the distribution of the difference of two Poisson random variables), and discrete Laplace and discrete normal distributions discretised by CDF differencing. Each comes in a fixed-location form, whose mean is structurally zero, and a free-location form that estimates the systematic disagreement between the two sources. All six are parameterised on a common mean and SD-scale convention, so that fits are directly comparable.

Every family supplies a Stan log-CCDF function as a stanvar, so that resp_trunc() normalises the likelihood correctly under truncation, including a row-varying bound. Fitting the asymmetric Skellam against the free-location discrete Laplace and discrete normal tests whether the disagreement obeys the Skellam variance-exceeds-absolute-mean constraint: the Skellam couples location and spread structurally, and the other two leave them independent.

Where the pair's overall level and the correlation between the two sources matter as well as their difference, model the pair jointly instead: see the companion package bicountbrms.

Documentation: https://anhsmith.github.io/skellambrms/
